one_month_reasoning: Two events fall in the window. Q3 2026 earnings are expected ~Oct 29; this is unconfirmed on the IR calendar, but past pattern is Oct 30 2025 and Oct 31 2024, so ~85-90% likely before the window ends Oct 30. FOMC meets Oct 27-28 after the Sep 16 hike, with another hike signalled. The Texas TCEQ compliance update is due Oct 19. Consensus Q3 EPS is ~$4.99 after hard upward revisions, so the bar is high. Industry read-across is mixed: MYR and Hubbell are strong, while MasTec fell 18.5% on a timing slip. Earnings-day moves have been large both ways (+17.3% on Q2-26, about -2.5% on Q3-25). I have no directional edge. The distribution is centred near spot (median ~$664) at monthly vol 44%/3.5 = 12.6%, with a 22% weight on a 1.6x-wider earnings-reaction component.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of forward P/E ($684 = Oct-2027 NTM EPS ~$22.4 x 30.5x) and EV/EBITDA ($658 = NTM EBITDA ~$5.33B x 20x = $106.6B EV, less ~$5.9B net debt, / 153M shares). Fair value ~$671, about 1% above spot.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus grown ~18%, matching the implied FY26-27 consensus growth. Supported by $53.4B backlog, +49% YoY against the matching quarter ($35.84B at 6/30/25), with 12-month backlog +61% ($32.3B vs $20.0B). Also supported by utility capex rising ~6-17%/yr and MYR seeing large 345-765kV jobs ramp in 2H27 into 2028. Equipment lead times (~128-week transformers) stretch the cycle rather than cut it. I risk ~3-5% of 2027 revenue slipping into 2028, which moves earnings between years rather than destroying them, so I make no EPS haircut in the base case and model the slip in the bear case.

PWR trades ~34-35x today, down from ~50x at end-June. Peers: EMCOR ~31x, Sterling ~43x, MasTec ~47x. Round 1 used 31x. I take off 1 turn for the Sep 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% (with another hike signalled), which pressures long-duration multiples, and add back ~0.5 turn because backlog growth is +49% rather than +36%, so earnings are more visible. Net 30.5x.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA as of Oct 2027 ~$5.33B x 20x = EV $106.6B; less net debt ~$5.9B; / 153M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus revenue x ~10.5% EBITDA margin (2026 guidance implies ~10.5%; management sees electric segment margins of 10-12% possible). 2028 grows ~15% on backlog conversion: large transmission and generation field work starts in 2H27.
Current EV ~$107B (662.6 x 152.4M shares + ~$5.6-5.9B net debt) / NTM EBITDA ~$4.64B is ~23x. I move it to 20x, consistent with the P/E de-rating (including the rates headwind) and peers.

inputs_detail.value: ~$5.6B at 6/30/26 ($6.10B debt - $0.51B cash; pro forma for the Aug notes, $7.0B debt - $1.4B cash); ~$5.9B assumed Oct-27
inputs_detail.derivation: The August notes refinanced CP and the revolver, so pro forma net debt stays about $5.6B. Add the July Enerfab payment. FCF of $2.0-2.5B/yr is roughly matched by continued M&A (~$1.2-1.5B+/yr) plus dividends and buybacks, so net debt holds at about $5.9B rather than falling to $5.0B as I assumed in round 1.
Slight creep from stock compensation and acquisition consideration.

bear.story: Several shocks hit together. Hyperscaler capex digests in 2027. The Texas TCEQ permit freeze (Sep 21) and moratoria in other states slow large-load interconnects. Transformer and GSU lead times of 128-144 weeks plus EO 14420 push ~5-8% of 2027-28 work to the right, the same timing slip MasTec was punished for. The Fed keeps hiking. NTM EPS ~$20 and the multiple falls to ~22x, the peer/pre-2023 level.

base.story: Backlog (+49% YoY, 12-month +61%) converts largely on schedule. 2027 EPS lands near $19.8-20 and large transmission and generation field work starts in 2H27, which MYR also sees. The multiple compresses to ~30.5x on NTM ~$22.5 as rates stay higher.

bull.story: Quanta keeps beating consensus (Q2 +28%). 12-month backlog of +61% converts into upside to 2027 numbers, hyperscaler 2027 capex lands near the high end ($1.1-1.2T), and labor scarcity gives Quanta pricing power. NTM EPS ~$24.5 at ~37.5x.

thesis_break_reason: $460 is ~31% below spot and ~23x FY27 consensus EPS ($19.77), the peer/pre-2023 multiple, and it sits above the $404.51 52-week low, which was set when backlog was ~$36-44B against $53.4B now. Getting there would most likely need a real fundamental break: a guidance cut, a sequential backlog decline, large programs slipping out of 2027, or a visible retrenchment in hyperscaler or utility capex (e.g. the Texas freeze spreading, rate cases rejected). A 44%-vol stock with rising estimates would not usually reach it on drift alone. I lowered it from $470 because the stronger backlog makes a fundamental break less likely at any given price, and the rates headwind means some multiple compression toward the high-$400s could be macro rather than a broken thesis.

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI data-center capex into 2027-28; direct exposure is only ~10% of revenue, but it drives utility load growth
How much backlog conversion slips because of transformer/GSU lead times (128-144 weeks) and EO 14420; I assume 3-5% of 2027 revenue in the base case, more in the bear case
How far the multiple de-rates while the Fed is hiking (3.75-4.00%, more signalled)

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks changed four inputs. (1) Backlog growth is +49% YoY, not +36%; I had compared against Sept-2025 ($39.2B) instead of June-2025 ($35.84B, confirmed in the Q2-25 release). 12-month backlog is +61%. This gives more support for FY27-28 earnings, but consensus already embeds much of it. (2) Net debt is ~$5.9B, not $5.0B, because the notes were refinancing (424B5) and Enerfab plus continued M&A absorbs FCF. That costs ~$4/share. (3) The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and signals more; I take ~1 turn off the P/E. (4) Direct data-center exposure is ~10% of revenue, so state moratoria, including the new Texas TCEQ freeze (Sep 21, no end date), hit mainly through utility load growth. I also quantified the timing risk the supervisor asked for. Transformer and GSU lead times are 128-144 weeks and MYR's large Xcel jobs ramp only in 2H27, so I assume ~3-5% of 2027 revenue could slip into 2028. That shifts earnings between years rather than destroying them, so it goes into the bear case rather than a base-case haircut. Valuation: P/E $684 (30.5x on NTM ~$22.4) and EV/EBITDA $658 (20x on ~$5.33B less $5.9B net debt), giving a blended $671 (round 1: $680). The analyst mean of ~$770 is higher. Scenarios: 22% at $440, 53% at $690, 25% at $920, mean ~$692. The ladder is a lognormal mixture with median ~$675: 85% at sigma 0.37 and 15% at sigma 0.65 for fat tails, roughly the 44% realized vol with heavier tails. P(>= $663) is ~0.52. Thesis break moves to $460. Research was limited to ~6 follow-up searches; X was not used.
